deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 43v is blank except for mirror-image show-through (or offset) of the ink text on the recto, 43r. The recto is a library borrowing slip. Read un-mirrored, it says: 'Journal de l'école polytechnique. Cahier 6 Paris an 7. / Cah. 15 1809 / Cah. 35-36. 1855 / B. Riemann / (Westfal)'. This is Riemann's request for three issues of the Journal de l'École polytechnique: Cahier 6 (an VII, i.e. 1798/99), Cahier 15 (1809) and Cahiers 35-36 (1855). The only marks original to the verso are a small red dot and a small red 'x' near the centre, and perhaps a faint pencil stroke at the top edge. These are probably library or archival marks. The next folio (44) is a similar slip, dated Nov. 1858 and signed 'B. Riemann', for a Hanoverian consistorial law collection. So these slips are bibliographic and biographical evidence of Riemann's reading around late 1858. They are not mathematical work. The page has no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Library loan slip (seen through the paper) requesting Journal de l'École polytechnique, Cahiers 6, 15 and 35-36

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics. It shows only the reversed text of a library request slip whose original is on the recto. That Riemann consulted the Journal de l'École polytechnique is unremarkable.
transcription_corrections: The whole text is mirror-image show-through of folio 43r, not independent writing on 43v. It should be read un-mirrored and treated as identical to the recto.
'Cahier 6 Tom. II.[?]' should read 'Cahier 6 Paris an 7.' In the mirrored image the right-hand entry is clearly 'Paris an 7' (Revolutionary year VII), matching the recto.
'Cah. 15 1809[?]' and 'Cah. 35-36. 1855[?]' are correct. The question marks can be dropped.
'E.[?] Riemann[?]' should be 'B. Riemann', the same signature as on the recto.
'(Weißfisch[?])' is the mirrored parenthetical word from the recto, transcribed there as '(Westfal)'. It is not a separate word.
The transcription omits a small red dot and a small red 'x' near the centre of the page. These are the only marks proper to the verso.
